keyFindings.description: The browser sentence this round added is false for Playwright, the browser this repository actually uses, and acting on it breaks the sharing the repository relies on. It says a browser download 'passes only if you point that tool's own cache variable at a directory under one of those paths yourself — the runtime sets no browser path at all, so an unset one leaves the download wherever the tool defaults, which is nowhere this runtime chose' (docs/kubernetes.md:236-238 says the same in its own words). playwright-core resolves its registry to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ms-playwright, and the runtime sets XDG_CACHE_HOME to /legion/scratch/cache, the issue's volume — which this very document states 2,060 lines below, unchanged by this diff: docs/kubernetes.md:2299-2305, 'Sharing the cache home gives the issue's roles one Playwright browser registry, since playwright-core resolves it to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ms-playwright, and Registry.install() takes an exclusive lock on that directory'. The literal half (no PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH or PUPPETEER_CACHE_DIR is set anywhere) is true; the inference drawn from it is not. A role that obeys it either escalates a sanctioned, volume-resident, issue-shared download to its architect for nothing, or points PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH somewhere of its own and leaves the shared registry and the install lock that keeps two roles of an issue from racing. And it is the browser the suite psql was added for runs: packages/dispatch/e2e/playwright.config.ts names Desktop Chrome, Firefox and WebKit with no executablePath or channel, so `bun run e2e` needs a registry install.

'Under one of those variables it is on the issue's volume: it outlives the pod, every role of the issue shares it, and a later pod of the issue reuses it' quantifies over the nine variables named one paragraph above, and is false for one of them. XDG_STATE_HOME is /legion/scratch/state/<role>: measured in this container it is .../state/reviewer, with sibling directories for implementer, planner and tester. The runtime says so itself at packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/manifest.go:741-749 — 'the one directory of the issue's scratch that is the role's own rather than the issue's' — and gives the reason, Oh My Pi's browser broker lock, which one shared state root would make every role but the first fail on. docs/kubernetes.md repeats the per-role fact in five further places this diff does not touch. A role sizing a download reads the sentence, puts the tool's cache under $XDG_STATE_HOME, and the siblings do not find it: one copy per role where the paragraph exists to teach one per issue. Same clause at docs/kubernetes.md:240. The fix is the one the paragraph already uses for XDG_CONFIG_HOME: exclude it by name.

The five-file instruction is incomplete and the reason it gives for trusting it is false. It says the image change 'carries the same name through five files, because its own tests hold them to each other', and names inside worker.Dockerfile only the apt line and its comment. Two further sites in that file are code, not comments, and no test holds either: worker.Dockerfile:417 is the THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES intro string, which assemble-third-party-notices.sh copies verbatim into /usr/share/doc/legion/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES in the shipped image and which hand-lists the Debian packages by name; and worker.Dockerfile:644 is the build's toolchain smoke step, `psql --version; redis-cli --version; sqlite3 --version; nc -h; dig -v`. A worker who follows the instruction adds a sixth tool, opens green, and ships an image whose licence file does not name the package it installs — a licence obligation, not a tidiness gap — with the new tool unexercised by the smoke step. Same text in AGENTS.md:125. Either name those two sites too, or say that the five are what the tests hold and that the Dockerfile's other enumerations must be carried by hand.

Reported, not requested: 'the wheel lands in UV_CACHE_DIR, the interpreter under UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR, and the issue's next pod finds both there'. Driven by the thermonuclear pair with uv 0.12.21, an empty cache and both variables pointed at a scratch directory: UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR took 70 MB of cpython-3.12.7, and UV_CACHE_DIR took 20 KB with no wheel — the interpreter archive is not cached and there is no wheel in the case the sentence describes. The verdict the sentence delivers (this install is sanctioned, because it lands under UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR on the issue's volume) is right, which is why this is reported rather than requested; the docs/kubernetes.md twin at :234-236 already omits the wheel clause, so the two copies have diverged on it.

threads: Twenty-five threads, all of rounds 1 to 4, every one carrying the implementer's disposition and resolved by it. I read round 4's five resolutions against the tree and accept them; I unresolved none. This round's three findings and one report are new threads.
acceptedThisRound: The second-order rule's terms are concrete: nine variables named with their paths, XDG_CONFIG_HOME excluded as the pod's shared in-memory volume (manifest.go:542 backs it with EmptyDir{Medium: Memory}), $HOME named as the container's own filesystem, and the cost stated as one copy per role per pod lost on relaunch. The handoff now records that the architect ruled the second-order case, so the artefacts no longer disagree.
sqlite3's reason is true in all four copies, with the session's real files named (results.jsonl, state.json, title under XDG_STATE_HOME) and the profile databases that genuinely are SQLite.
The image-change instruction names the Go sites and why each is required — incomplete only in the Dockerfile half, which is finding 3.
tools.md:9 carries the digest-roll condition with `command -v` as the check; this pod is the case it predicts, since all five are missing here.
dig -v corrected to stdout with the measurement that settles it.
verifiedMyself: docs/kubernetes.md:2299-2305 states that playwright-core resolves its registry to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/ms-playwright and that Registry.install() locks it — the sentence finding 1 contradicts.
XDG_STATE_HOME is /legion/scratch/state/reviewer with sibling per-role directories; manifest.go:741-749 calls it the one directory of the scratch that is the role's own.
worker.Dockerfile:417 is the notices intro string and :644 the smoke step, both code naming the five tools, neither gated by a test.

pattern: Three rounds running, the findings are new false statements introduced by the previous round's correction, in the same ~170 lines of prose kept by hand in two files and a generated third. That is no longer an argument for a follow-up: the structural split is now cheaper than another clause round, and it is the architect's call on scope rather than a request of mine.
fastFollow: Give one file canonical ownership of the runner forms, the transcripts and the sanctioned/withheld jurisprudence — tools.md the forms and the rule a role types against, docs/kubernetes.md the decision, the options table and the measurements — and have the other cite rather than restate.
